[]

Do NOT comment on:
- Missing or insufficient test coverage
- Style, formatting, naming, or readability preferences
- Documentation gaps or comment wording
- Refactoring suggestions, alternative designs, or speculative "could be cleaner" feedback
- Praise or restating what the code does

Do NOT invent issues. If the diff is clean, return zero comments. It is correct and expected to return an empty comments array on branches without real problems. Do not pad output with weak or borderline findings.

1. git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat
2. git diff origin/main...HEAD
3. git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline

Flag as a functional gap / missing guard, not a style issue.

The `summary` field MUST be an empty string. The review body's header is generated deterministically by the system; do not write a prose summary.

Each comment MUST have:
- `severity`: exactly one of `high`, `medium`, or `low`
- `confidence`: a number between 0 and 1 (inclusive) for how certain you are this is a real, actionable issue. Use 0.9+ only when you are highly confident.
- `body`: GitHub-flavored markdown in 1–3 short sentences explaining the issue, its impact, and what to change. Reference symbols and file names in backticks. Do not include title/severity headings.
- `location`: `{ "granularity": "line", "file_path": "<final file path>", "start_line": <final right-side line number> }`

Use `granularity: "range"` with `end_line` only when the full finding genuinely spans multiple changed right-side lines. Prefer a single changed line.

Output ONLY this JSON object as the very last line:

{"summary":"","comments":[{"severity":"<high|medium|low>","confidence":<0-1>,"body":"<concise comment>","location":{"granularity":"line","file_path":"<file path>","start_line":<final right-side line number>}}]}

If there are no actionable findings, output: {"summary":"","comments":[]}

- dev: TDD Developer agent - implements features using test-driven development and clean code principles (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- agent-integration: Run all three agent integration phases sequentially: research, write-tests, and implement using E2E-first TDD (unit tests written last). For individual phases, use /agent-integration:research, /agent-integration:write-tests, or /agent-integration:implement. Use when the user says "integrate agent", "add agent support", or wants to run the full agent integration pipeline end-to-end.
- changelog: Generate or update the CHANGELOG.md for a new release version. Use when the user says "generate changelog", "update changelog", "write release notes", or asks to prepare a changelog for a version like "changelog for 0.5.3".

For individual phases, use /e2e:triage-ci, /e2e:debug, or /e2e:implement. Use when the user says "triage e2e", "fix e2e failures", or wants the full triage-to-fix pipeline.
- test-repo: Use this skill to test strategy changes against a fresh test repository. Invoke when the user asks to "test against a test repo", "validate the changes", or wants to verify session hooks, commits, and rewind functionality work correctly.
- analyst: Requirements analyst agent - gathers, clarifies, and documents requirements
- dev: TDD Developer agent - implements features using test-driven development and clean code principles
- dev-cycle: Orchestrates the development cycle - developer implements, reviewer critiques, repeat until done
- reviewer: Code review agent - critically reviews changes for quality, security, and correctness
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

54	const (
55		loginURLNone loginURLAction = iota
56		loginURLCopy
57		loginURLOpen
58	)
59	
60	type loginURLActionReadFunc func(ctx context.Context) (loginURLAction, error)
61	
62	// clipboardCopyTimeout bounds a single clipboard write. See copyLoginURL.
63	const clipboardCopyTimeout = 3 * time.Second
64	
65	// loginURLInteractor owns the side effects behind the interactive URL prompt.
66	// Production uses the controlling TTY, system clipboard, and default browser;
67	// tests provide deterministic functions instead. keysAvailable answers whether
68	// readAction can actually deliver keys, so the prompt only advertises actions
69	// this process can honour.
70	type loginURLInteractor struct {
71		keysAvailable func() bool
72		readAction    loginURLActionReadFunc
73		copyURL       clipboardWriteFunc
74		openURL       browserOpenFunc
75	}
76	
77	func defaultLoginURLInteractor(errW io.Writer) loginURLInteractor {
78		return loginURLInteractor{
79			keysAvailable: loginURLKeysAvailable,
80			readAction: func(ctx context.Context) (loginURLAction, error) {
81				return readLoginURLAction(ctx, errW)
82			},
83			copyURL: clipboard.WriteAll,
84			openURL: openBrowser,
85		}
86	}
87	
88	// loginURLKeysAvailable reports whether single-key actions can be read from the
89	// controlling terminal. It mirrors exactly the conditions under which
90	// readLoginURLAction gives up and returns loginURLNone, so the prompt is never
91	// printed for keys that would be ignored.
92	func loginURLKeysAvailable() bool {
93		if interactive.UnderTest() {
94			return false
95		}
96	
97		tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
98		if err != nil {
99			return false
100		}
101		defer tty.Close()
102	
103		return interactive.IsTerminalReader(tty)
104	}
105	
106	// copyLoginURL bounds a clipboard write. clipboardWriteFunc takes no context —
107	// atotto/clipboard shells out to xclip/xsel on Linux — so a wedged helper would
108	// otherwise block the select loop in waitForLoginURLResult indefinitely, and
109	// with it a sign-in that has already completed. On timeout the goroutine is
110	// abandoned; the CLI is short-lived and exits soon after.
111	func copyLoginURL(copyURL clipboardWriteFunc, loginURL string, timeout time.Duration) error {
112		done := make(chan error, 1)
113		go func() { done <- copyURL(loginURL) }()
114	
115		select {
116		case err := <-done:
117			return err
118		case <-time.After(timeout):
119			return fmt.Errorf("clipboard write timed out after %v", timeout)
120		}
121	}

124	// browser lands on a URL with the user_code already in the query string —
125	// most verification pages prefill the input from that param, sparing the
126	// user from typing. Falls back to the bare verification_uri when the AS
127	// didn't supply a complete form.
128	func chooseApprovalURL(start *auth.DeviceAuthStart) string {
129		if start.VerificationURIComplete != "" {
130			return start.VerificationURIComplete
131		}
132		return start.VerificationURI
133	}

136	type deviceAuthClient interface {
137		StartDeviceAuth(ctx context.Context) (*auth.DeviceAuthStart, error)
138		PollDeviceAuth(ctx context.Context, deviceCode string) (*auth.DeviceAuthPoll, error)
139		BaseURL() string
140	}

143	// login so runBrowserLogin can be unit-tested with a fake instead of a real
144	// listener. *auth.BrowserAuthFlow satisfies it.
145	type browserAuthFlow interface {
146		AuthorizationURL() string
147		Wait(ctx context.Context) (code string, err error)
148		Exchange(ctx context.Context, code string) (accessToken, refreshToken string, err error)
149		Close() error
150	}
151	
152	func newLoginCmd() *cobra.Command {
153		var (
154			insecureHTTPAuth bool
155			useDevice        bool
156			server           string
157		)
158		cmd := &cobra.Command{
159			Use:   "login",
160			Short: "Log in to Entire",
161			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
162				loginServer, err := parseLoginServer(server)
163				if err != nil {
164					return fmt.Errorf("invalid --server: %w", err)
165				}
166				if err := requireSecureLoginServer(loginServer, insecureHTTPAuth); err != nil {
167					return err
168				}
169				client := auth.NewClient(loginServer, nil, insecureHTTPAuth)
170				// Closure adapts the concrete *auth.BrowserAuthFlow result to the
171				// browserAuthFlow interface (func types are invariant, so the
172				// method value alone won't do). On error the flow is a typed nil,
173				// which is fine — runLoginAuto checks err before touching it.
174				startBrowser := func(ctx context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error) {
175					return client.StartBrowserAuth(ctx)
176				}
177				return runLoginAuto(cmd.Context(), cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
178					client, startBrowser, defaultLoginURLInteractor(cmd.ErrOrStderr()), loginFlowFacts{
179						useDevice:  useDevice,
180						canPrompt:  interactive.CanPromptInteractively(),
181						sshSession: isSSHSession(),
182					})
183			},
184		}
185		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&server, "server", api.DefaultAuthBaseURL,
186			"login server to authenticate against (rarely needed; the default serves all standard accounts)")
187		addInsecureHTTPAuthFlag(cmd, &insecureHTTPAuth)
188		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&useDevice, "device", false, "Use the device-code flow (enter a code in your browser) instead of the default browser redirect")
189		return cmd
190	}
191	
192	// parseLoginServer validates and canonicalises the --server value: an
193	// http(s) origin with nothing but scheme and host. Userinfo, path, query,
194	// and fragment are rejected rather than silently dropped — the value
195	// becomes the OAuth issuer, the token-exchange target, and the keyring
196	// key, so surprising rewrites would surface as confusing auth failures
197	// much later. A lone trailing slash is tolerated (normalised away).
198	func parseLoginServer(raw string) (string, error) {
199		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
200		if raw == "" {
201			return "", errors.New("empty server URL")
202		}
203		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
204		if err != nil {
205			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse server URL: %w", err)
206		}
207		// Error messages echo u.Redacted(), not raw: the URL may carry
208		// userinfo (that's one of the rejection cases), and stderr often ends
209		// up in CI logs where a password must not appear.
210		switch {
211		case u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP:
212			return "", fmt.Errorf("scheme must be http or https, got %q", u.Redacted())
213		case u.Host == "":
214			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing host in %q", u.Redacted())
215		case u.User != nil:
216			return "", fmt.Errorf("userinfo not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
217		case u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/":
218			return "", fmt.Errorf("path not allowed in %q (use the bare origin)", u.Redacted())
219		case u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "":
220			return "", fmt.Errorf("query/fragment not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
221		}
222		return api.NormalizeOriginURL(raw), nil
223	}
224	
225	// requireSecureLoginServer enforces TLS for the chosen login server — the
226	// only host login dials. --insecure-http-auth opts in to http:// (and
227	// enables it process-wide for the token save path).
228	func requireSecureLoginServer(server string, insecureHTTPAuth bool) error {
229		if insecureHTTPAuth {
230			auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()
231			return nil
232		}
233		if err := api.RequireSecureURL(server); err != nil {
234			return fmt.Errorf("login server check: %w", err)
235		}
236		return nil
237	}
238	
239	func runLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, client deviceAuthClient, urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, canPrompt bool) error {
240		start, err := client.StartDeviceAuth(ctx)
241		if err != nil {
242			return fmt.Errorf("start login: %w", err)
243		}
244	
245		approvalURL := chooseApprovalURL(start)
246		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Device code: %s\n", start.UserCode)
247		printLoginURL(outW, deviceLoginURLLabel, approvalURL)
248	
249		wait := func(waitCtx context.Context) (loginTokens, error) {
250			accessToken, refreshToken, waitErr := waitForApproval(
251				waitCtx,
252				client,
253				start.DeviceCode,
254				start.ExpiresIn,
255				time.Duration(start.Interval)*time.Second,
256				defaultSlowDownBackoff,
257			)
258			return loginTokens{accessToken: accessToken, refreshToken: refreshToken}, waitErr
259		}
